title: About
text:
Biography
I am an independent researcher and retired statistician. My research sits at the intersection of complexity science, social simulation, and retirement and pension systems, with a continuing interest in well-being measurement and official statistics.
My current work treats retirement timing as an emergent property of a complex adaptive system. The core is an agent-based model in which workers with hedonic, gain and normative goal frames (Goal-Framing Theory) respond to pension incentives through an option-value mechanism. The model is implemented in NetLogo, driven from R, with a mean-field companion system and a partial translation to Julia/Agents.jl. This work began in the International Doctoral Programme in Complexity Sciences (Iscte-IUL / FCUL). The programme was discontinued in 2025; I am completing the dissertation, Dynamics of Retirement Pension Systems: A Generational Approach, independently, preparing papers from it for journals in social simulation and retirement research, and exploring routes for submitting and defending it.
I worked at Statistics Portugal (INE) from 1990 to 2024. In the Department of Demographic and Social Statistics I was responsible for the production of the Well-being Index of Portugal and led the revision of the National Gender Database, and I was a member of the UNECE Task Force on Measurement of Well-being (2023–2024). Earlier I coordinated the Eurostat project ESSnet on SDMX: Metadata Common Vocabulary Ontology, sat on the SDMX Metadata Task Force (Eurostat) and the Common Metadata Framework Task Force (UNECE), took part in the European project Rainbow — An Object Network for Statisticians and Administrators, and headed the studies and dissemination unit of INE’s North Directorate.
I taught social research methods, statistics and organisational behaviour for more than twenty years at the Faculty of Economics of the University of Porto and at the Instituto Superior de Serviço Social do Porto.

title: Sérgio Bacelar
text:
Welcome
I am an independent researcher and retired statistician, based in Porto. I work on retirement and pension systems as complex adaptive systems, using agent-based modelling and social simulation.
My doctoral research, begun in the International Doctoral Programme in Complexity Sciences (Iscte-IUL / FCUL), models retirement timing as an emergent property of interacting workers, pension rules and demographic change. The programme was discontinued in 2025; I am completing the dissertation, Dynamics of Retirement Pension Systems: A Generational Approach, independently.
Before that I spent 34 years at Statistics Portugal (INE), most recently responsible for the Well-being Index of Portugal.
